rationale: The validation report explicitly reports issue=='golden_rejected': evaluate.py rejects the golden secure solution with a linker error 'undefined reference to conditional_swap' during FR4's g++ link step. The golden implements conditional_swap(uint32_t*, uint32_t*, int, unsigned int) exactly per the pinned public_spec.interface signature, so this is not a golden defect -- it is a build/link mismatch in evaluate.py or evaluation/harness_main.cpp (likely extern "C" linkage mismatch between harness_main.cpp's declaration/call site and the plain C++ linkage of the submitted translation unit, or an incorrect compile/link command that fails to combine harness_main.cpp and inputs/ladder_swap.cpp into one link step). Because the golden cannot even link, mutation_baseline_run never succeeds, mutation_score is 0.0 and explicitly flagged not meaningful, and mutation_status is blocked_by_differential -- discrimination_coverage is 0.0 accordingly. Separately, the validation report also flags issue=='requirement_id_mismatch' for SR3: evaluate.py never emits a [TEST] PASS/FAIL marker for SR3 on the golden run, breaking marker-completeness needed for grading. Both are evaluation harness defects, not specification or artifact defects; mapping_coverage=1.0 and analyzer's public_security_leak-style requirement passed, so the spec/case artifacts are otherwise sound. Per the golden_rejected and requirement_id_mismatch rules, evaluation_framework must be revised.
revision_instructions: Two concrete defects in the evaluation harness must be fixed, verified against the pinned interface `void conditional_swap(uint32_t *P, uint32_t *Q, int n, unsigned int ctrl_bit);` from public_spec.interface: (1) Fix the link failure causing golden_rejected on FR4. evaluate.py currently fails with 'undefined reference to `conditional_swap'' when linking harness_main.cpp against the submission -- this means the harness's declaration/call of conditional_swap and the submission's definition disagree on linkage or the build command does not actually compile+link both translation units together. Do not assume any particular internal styling of the submission; the check must only rely on the exact pinned signature. Ensure harness_main.cpp declares conditional_swap with plain C++ (non-extern-"C") linkage matching a normal C++17 translation unit defining that exact signature, and ensure evaluate.py's g++ invocation compiles evaluation/harness_main.cpp together with inputs/ladder_swap.cpp into a single linked executable (e.g. `g++ -std=c++17 -Wall -Wextra evaluation/harness_main.cpp inputs/ladder_swap.cpp -o <bin>`), not as separately linked objects with mismatched declarations. Any correct implementation of the pinned signature must link and run successfully -- grade this by actually compiling and executing the binary, never by matching source text. (2) Fix the missing SR3 marker: audit evaluate.py's control flow so that the SR3 timing-differential check (run conditional_swap many times for ctrl_bit=0 vs ctrl_bit=1 at fixed n, compare median timings against a generous threshold) is always invoked and always emits a `[TEST] PASS: SR3 ...` or `[TEST] FAIL: SR3 ...` marker with id exactly 'SR3', even if earlier checks failed or an exception occurred in an earlier stage -- wrap requirement checks so one failure does not skip subsequent ones, and ensure the SR3 marker id matches the requirement_map id character-for-character. After both fixes, re-run the differential: the golden must produce all-PASS markers for FR1-FR4 and SR1-SR3, and the shipped insecure baseline (branch on ctrl_bit) must FAIL specifically on SR1/SR2/SR3 (not on FR4), confirming real security discrimination before mutation scoring is attempted again.
